# Compose & send

Composing in Envoir looks like any modern mail client, with two things bolted directly into the
compose window instead of hidden in a menu: **who can see this message travel** (the privacy
tier) and **exactly what "send" does under the hood** (a plain-language note that changes with
your network mode). This page walks through the compose window end to end.

![Compose — recipients, privacy tier, and the honest send note](assets/screens/compose-dark.png)

## Opening compose

Three ways in: the **Compose** button (top-right or the mail rail), the `c` keyboard shortcut from
anywhere in the app, or **Reply**/**Forward** from an open conversation (which pre-fills the
recipient and subject).

## Filling in the message

- **To** — type a `name@domain` address, a bare key-name, a `.eth`/`.sol` name-chain address, an
  `@handle`, or a [group](#groups) address. As you type, an autocomplete list resolves against
  your contacts and shows which naming rung each match is on.
- **Subject** and a **rich-text body** — bold/italic/lists, and file attachments via the paperclip
  (each attachment shows its name and size as a removable chip).
- **Privacy tier** — a segmented control right in the compose footer:
  - **Private** (shield icon) — the metadata-private mixnet path (see
    [Privacy & threat model](#privacy)). This is the default.
  - **Fast** — the direct path, lower latency, no metadata protection beyond content encryption.

  This is a real, per-message choice, not a setting buried three menus deep — because the tradeoff
  (privacy vs. speed) is something you might genuinely want to make differently for different
  messages.

## Draft autosave

Envoir autosaves your draft as you type — stop typing for a moment and it upserts into the
**Drafts** folder without you doing anything. Close the compose window at any point and your
in-progress message is waiting for you in Drafts, not lost. Re-opening a draft resumes editing
exactly where you left off.

## Scheduling a send

Click the clock icon to reveal quick options — "tomorrow morning," "Monday morning" — or pick a
custom time. Once scheduled, the **Send** button becomes **Schedule**, and the message waits in a
scheduled state until that time (visible with a clock badge on its conversation row); you can
still edit or cancel it before it goes.

## Sending, and undo send

Click **Send**. In this reference client (with no real node connected — see
[Settings & devices](#settings#node-connection-leaving-the-demo-behind) for connecting one), the message moves into Sent
immediately, with a brief **undo** window in the toast that appears — click it in time and the
send is reverted, the draft restored. Once a real node is connected with a send capability
provisioned, "send" instead calls the node's real Send API and the composed message travels for
real; the compose footer's own note tells you plainly which of the two is about to happen before
you click.

## What the honest send note means

The line of text just above the Send button (visible whenever you have a node connected) changes
with your setup:

- **Simulated** — no node connected; sending updates the local demo data only.
- **Seam** — a node is connected and syncing your real mailbox, but no send capability token has
  been provisioned yet, so compose refuses to fake a send rather than silently pretending it
  worked.
- **Real** — a node is connected *and* a send token is provisioned; clicking Send calls the node's
  actual `POST /v1/send` and a real, end-to-end-encrypted MOTE is sealed and dispatched.

This note exists specifically so the client never claims a message was sent when it wasn't — see
[Settings & devices](#settings#node-connection-leaving-the-demo-behind) for wiring up a real node.

## Programmatic sending — Envoir Send

A [`CapabilityToken`](https://github.com/vul-os/kotva/blob/main/crates/kotva-core/src/capability.rs) is a signed, offline-verifiable,
chainable grant of one narrow `(resource, ability, caveats)` right — real and tested in
`dmtap-core` today. The natural application built on it is **Envoir Send**, a Resend-style
programmatic mail-sending API: mint a narrowly-scoped, send-only capability per API key, and a
compromised or retired key is one revocation away from being worthless, without ever touching your
root identity. This is a sovereign, self-hostable alternative to a hosted transactional-email API
— the capability primitive is shipped and tested today, but the dedicated send-service crate isn't
part of this workspace yet. See [Protocol](#protocol#delegated-capabilities-and-envoir-send)
and [Roadmap](#roadmap).

## What's real vs. simulated today

Draft construction, autosave, scheduling logic, and the tier picker are real client code. Whether
"Send" actually dispatches a MOTE depends entirely on your network mode, as described above — see
[Roadmap](#roadmap) for the project-wide real-vs-simulated line.
